name: Maol Flidais

the wildwood goddess who owned the cow Maol Flidais

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Maol Flidais was an Irish mythological figure. Like the great Glas Ghaibhleann, the cow that gave endless milk, Maol Flidais was a symbol of abundance. The wildwood goddess Flidais owned this beast. The cow may originally have been a goddess herself, for she was described as equal to her mistress. Maol Flidais gave milk freely. Her gentle lowing was said to carry across the land.
objective: Document Maol Flidais, the Irish cow of abundance owned by the goddess Flidais.
